coverage_note: Lesson is Arabic-with-English throughout; long English stretches 03:40-05:51 (recording-rule talk), 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:00, 57:37-1:02:33 (causative-verb discussion). Amal's lines are Arabic script; no chat lines in this file. Echo: 'Intayn ila tult' (07:20) = تنتين إلا تلت; 'Asha tisa alfayn situation' (06:47) = عشرة تسعة ألفين ستة وعشرين; engine wrote بدائية (12:13) for Amal's وردانية, ليش ما (16:06) for ليش مع, فعلاً (13:42) for فعلين, بتطلّي (32:45) for بتضلي, نوع الإل (38:33) for بدون الـ, كساته (39:58) for كاساته, أزت/أزد (24:12-24:25) for قصد, صحته (42:15) for صح, بفيت (55:30) unreadable, أنا واعي (55:33) unclear. Left out as S4 pronunciation: جهزت -> her وجهّزت (03:13, shadda only), أزعشتك (15:02, ج->ش), بعيم for بقيم (26:54), أجر for إجر (35:45), the dropped ق in بيتايوكي (25:08; the b- part is filed), إشي vowel (52:52). Six letter-order (dyslexia) slips that Amal voiced ARE written as low-confidence vocab-A tier 2 rows (02:49 زعمت, 27:50 بخسر, 29:46 سكرتي, 34:14 إسكر, 43:00 انسكرت, 52:36 سكرت) because Medi at 04:05 himself expects زعمت to be marked wrong - the judge should rule whether S4 excludes them. Self-fixes skipped: 13:37 بنزعوج -> بزعج/بنزعج, 35:38 تكرت -> كسرت, 57:14 أكسر -> بكسر. Questions not scored: 36:58 'is it نكسر?', 44:51 'is it بنكسر?', 31:20 'was it بتكسر?', 43:32 'كان عمرها or عمرها كان? كانت' (Amal: both, كان عمرها better; لا to كانت). English 'air conditioning' inside Arabic (07:39, 12:53, 53:10) is not on her sheet (Amal uses the English word herself at 48:29) so not tier 3; 'bones' (51:20) not on sheet. Names: Amal / أمل.

rows.why: He said za3amt (letters swapped) for 3azamt (I invited); Amal said 'jarreb kam marra' then supplied عزمت and he repeated it; letter-order slip may fall under S4 root-letter slip, but Medi himself at 04:05 cites this as the word that should be marked wrong - judge to rule.

rows.medi_said: تسعة asha. Oh no, that's right. Yeah, asha tisa.
rows.why: For the date he said the month before the day (tis3a 3ashra); Amal: 'first we say' 3ashra tis3a - day then month; engine wrote 'alfayn situation' = ألفين ستة وعشرين.

rows.medi_said: سـ... تلات إلا نـ... إلا تلت.
rows.why: Asked 2addesh el-saa3a he answered tlaat illa tult; Amal asked 'three or two?', he fixed to tintayn illa tult (engine wrote 'Intayn ila tult') and she confirmed; may be a fact fix (the actual hour) rather than language, or the clock number form.
He stretched the vowel (salaa7to) for salla7to 'I fixed it'; Amal recast صلحته and he repeated صلاحتو again at 08:12; vowel-length (F2, pronunciation family) not scored on its own.

rows.medi_said: Is it را-- راكي؟ What, What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked what electricity was and Amal supplied كهربا (sheet: electricity | Kahraba | كهربا).

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: In the idafa 'engineer of the electricity' the last word takes el-: muhandis el-kahraba; he left it bare, but he framed it as a question ('do you guys say'), so it may be a question not a slip.

rows.amal_said: Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
rows.why: New word taught: Amal offered كهربجي (electrician) which he had never attempted; he then tried to combine it with مهندس.

rows.medi_said: كراجي. See, This is a new word.
rows.why: His repeat of the brand-new word came out as karaaji (also kerhabji at 09:30); Amal recast kahrabji; likely a sound slip on a word just learned.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- لا، أه، كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: Trying to say the electrician is / is not an engineer he used ma ykoon before a noun; a noun sentence is negated with mish; Amal let it pass (reading of a broken line).
rows.english: he is not an engineer, he is an electrician

rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed.
rows.why: He hung the object on the verb (salla7ni = he fixed ME); 'he fixed FOR me' puts the person on li-: salla7 li (10:30, 10:51 'Fixed for me, صلح لي').
rows.english: he fixed (it) for me a bit

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلح (fix) meaning 'helped'; Amal: 'you said sala7 which is fix, did you want to say he helped me?' and he produced ساعدني at 11:07, she confirmed (sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد).
Feminine noun blouse took a masculine colour adjective; Amal recast wardaaniyye (engine wrote بدائية) and he repeated وردانية 'that's right'.
He said dawlat for dallait (I stayed); Amal said 'what?' then ضليت and he repeated it; sound/vowel shape of a word he knows (sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | ضليت).

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take على بيتي.
rows.why: 'At home' takes bi/fi, not 3ala; Amal prompted 'bi or fi?' and he fixed to في بيتي.
'One word': the number-adjective wa7de goes after the noun; he put it first, Amal recast kilme wa7de.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: 'Two verbs' is the dual fi3lein, not fi3l + tnein; Amal recast (engine wrote فعلاً for فعلين) and he said فعلين at 13:46.
inza3aj takes min (annoyed FROM me), Amal had said so at 14:35; he used ma3i, she asked 'leish ma3?' (engine wrote ليش ما) and he fixed to انزعجتي مني at 16:22 - 'Perfect'.
He calqued 'one more' as wa7ad aktar; Amal recast kaman wa7ad and he repeated it (sheet: some more / another | Kaman | كمان); framed as a question so may be a question not a slip.
Talking to a woman (inti) he used the masculine participle; Amal prompted 'inti or inta?' and he fixed to مزعوجة.
Plural subject (many things) needs the plural verb biz3ajuni; he used a singular form, Amal recast and he repeated the slip at 20:29 then took بيزعجوني at 20:33 (same moment).
rows.english: many things annoy me these days

rows.why: Plural of yom is ayyaam; he produced el-ayoom, Amal recast and he said 'I even wrote ayyaam'.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: After hadol the noun keeps its el- (he had it at 20:41 then dropped it); Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: إنتي متأكدة إلي إنتو ما ازعج، ازعجتو.
rows.why: 'Sure THAT you didn't annoy him' is inno; he used illi (the one that); Amal asked 'why illi?' and said 'inno, mish illi'.
rows.english: are you sure that you (pl) didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'You didn't annoy HIM' needs the object ending -o on the verb; he left it off and Amal only addressed the illi.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: iza keeps the b- on the verb; he dropped it (ashoofak), Amal recast bashoof and he repeated إذا ما بشوفك مبسوطة; his 'is it tkooni or just mabsoota?' was a question, answered 'bas mabsoota'.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I don't see you happy

rows.why: For 'don't be annoyed' he gave a bare command; Amal prompted 'so don't be' and he built ما تنزعج / ما تنزعجي which she echoed.
After 'mish 2asdhom' (they didn't mean to) the next verb loses its b-: ydaay2uki; he kept the b- (and dropped the 2 - sound); Amal recast; his أزدهم at 24:25 is 2asdhom misheard/mangled.
rows.english: they didn't mean to upset you

rows.medi_said: So I add is بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: Groping for 'I add' he produced bziyaad; Amal supplied bzeed and he repeated it.
Didn't-know: he asked for the verb 'remove' and Amal gave b2eem.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: 'The first (part) of the verb' is an idafa: awwal el-fi3l - the first word never takes el-; he put el- on both; Amal let it pass.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / word

rows.why: He built 'I break' as ba5sar (a different word, lose); Amal: 'close - baksar'; a root-letter swap that may be S4, written for the judge.
Letters swapped: sakkarti (you closed) for kasarti (you broke); Amal recast and he repeated شو كسرتي; letter-order slip, maybe S4, written for the judge.
After btdalli (you keep) the second verb keeps its b-; he said kasri without it, Amal recast بتكسري, 'I didn't hear the t', and he gave بتكسري at 33:31 (engine wrote بتطلّي for بتضلي).

rows.medi_said: Is it يسكر and يسكري؟ اسكرو؟ إسكر.
rows.amal_said: The K is before the S.
rows.why: Command 'break': he swapped the letters (iskar); Amal: 'the K is before the S' and he fixed to اكسري، اكسروا; letter-order slip, maybe S4, written for the judge.
A noun carrying a possessive ending never takes el-; he said el-ashyaa2i, Amal said ashyaa2i without the el (engine 'نوع الإل' = bidoon el-) and he repeated كل أشيائي.
'His cups' is the plural kaasaato; he said the singular kaasto; Amal recast and he said كاساته 'of course'.
kaas has no ta-marbuta, so 'his cup' is kaaso, not kaasto; Amal recast كاسه, he repeated كاسته at 40:35 (same moment) and she said كاسه انكسرت at 40:46.
kaas is feminine so the verb is inkasarat; he used the masculine; Amal recast, he asked انكسرت؟ and then 'Oh, cause it's female'.

rows.amal_said: صح، بس order. Word or letters order.
rows.why: Letters swapped in inkasarat; Amal asked him to say it again then 'bas order... letters order' and he fixed to انكسرت; letter-order slip, maybe S4, written for the judge.
The sentence was 'when she was 12'; he said eleven; Amal recast itnaash and he used it at 44:18; may be a lapse of the number rather than the word.
He gave the huwwe form for hiyye; Amal said 'huwwe' and he fixed to هي بتنكسر; his بينكسري at 45:24 was the same stumble.

rows.medi_said: air condition-ي، air conditioner-ي. Do I say for air condition?
rows.why: A possessive ending does not go on a foreign word; it takes el- + taba3i; he tried '-i' then asked and Amal supplied the form, which he repeated.

rows.amal_said: مم، here's the thing. If it's physically broke then it's this. If it's not working properly we'd need that other word if you remember it.
rows.why: inkasar is physical breaking; an air conditioner that stops working is 5arbaan / 5ireb (sheet: not working properly | 5arbaan | خربان); he recalled خربان at 48:58, repeated إن كسر من الحرارة at 49:28 (same moment).

rows.medi_said: بكسور-- بكسر، أنا ما بكسر، اشي، إجري on my body. على إجري.
rows.why: 'I never broke anything' is past kasart; he used present baksar thinking abadan forces it; Amal 'baksar or kasart?', 'no, who said that?' and he fixed to أنا أبدًا ما كسرت ولا اشي at 52:44.
rows.english: I never broke anything on my body

rows.why: Letters swapped again (sakkart for kasart); Amal recast and he said كسرت at 52:44; letter-order slip, maybe S4, written for the judge.
The negation goes on the verb with ma; he put mish on the adverb; Amal offered 'or ma nimt mnee7' and he repeated it - she said 'or', so she may be treating both as fine.

rows.medi_said: إن إن. الفـ--، الفـ--، علات، الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Plural of fi3l is the broken plural af3aal; he invented fi3laat; Amal recast and he said الأفعال.
'I am annoyed' is the passive participle maz3ooj; he gave the active maz3ij (annoying), said 'No' but had no right word before Amal supplied أنا مزعوج; B15 not taught - file, not counted.
